lede: A blowout October payrolls report (+165k vs ~60k expected, jobless rate 4.1%) lifted the dollar index about 0.8% on Friday and pushed markets to price a December Fed hike as the likelier outcome. Gold, EUR/USD and GBP/USD closed the week lower on the day, tech stocks recovered part of Thursday's rout, and bitcoin is drifting near $75.8k over the weekend.
snapshot_time: Fri 6 Nov close (forex & gold closed for the weekend)

focus.text: Ended Friday near $4,071 (−0.4%) as strong jobs data lifted the dollar and yields, yet still logged its best week in over two months. Opens Monday right at its 4,068 pivot; US CPI on Tuesday is the week's key risk.
Fell 0.7% to 1.1142, near Friday's 1.1131 low, after payrolls revived Fed-hike bets. Sits below the 1.1169 pivot going into Monday; Tuesday's US CPI (16:30 TRT) is the main test.

technicals.indicators: Back above 20-day MA · 61.8% Fib ≈ 3,975 · Mon pivot 4,068
technicals.note: Thursday's channel breakout stalled at 4,147 and Friday pulled back to retest the former resistance zone near 4,030–4,080 from above.

technicals.indicators: MACD negative but above signal · below middle Bollinger band
technicals.note: Two failures near 1.1270 this week were followed by Friday's slide to the bottom of the 1.11–1.13 range.
Price is trapped between the falling 20/50-day averages above and the 200-day SMA below, after losing the $80k area earlier in the week.
Friday's modest bounce held above Thursday's 7,346 low but stayed well below the 7,737 level where Thursday's sell-off began.

news.text: US employers added 165k jobs in October, nearly three times forecasts; unemployment eased to 4.1% and wage growth picked up to 3.1% y/y.
Prediction markets put the odds of a December Fed rate hike near 78% after the data; the 10-year yield closed about 4.86%.
S&P 500 rose 0.3% and Nasdaq 1.1% as chipmakers bounced, but the index lost about 2.7% on the week; the Dow slipped 0.5%.
Japan's Nikkei and Korea's Kospi each dropped about 6% Friday on worries over AI regulation, extending the global chip sell-off.
Brent eased 0.5% to about $97.8 and WTI to $90.4, with traders weighing uncertain Iran-related diplomacy.
US spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $430M on Thursday; BlackRock's IBIT has now lost over $1B across five straight sessions of outflows.
Bitcoin ETFs' net flows for 2026 have turned negative, at roughly −$500M year to date, wiping out all inflows logged this year.
FinCEN and the Federal Reserve dropped a plan to cut the reporting threshold for cross-border crypto transfers from $3,000 to $250.
More than $1.1B of leveraged long positions were wiped out over 5–6 Nov as bitcoin fell from above $80k to below $76k.
The Fear & Greed index sank to 28 from 50; bitcoin dominance stands near 59% and ETH/BTC slipped to 0.0294.
XRP lagged with a ~3% drop to $1.17 and Bitcoin Cash was the weakest top-100 coin (−4.5%), while SOL steadied near $90.
